## Economic History

**Prague University of Economics and Business**  
Department of Economic History

The course introduces the long-run transformation of economic institutions and the historical foundations of modern growth, industrialisation, monetary systems, crises, and economic policy. My teaching contribution links historical narrative to the interpretation of evidence and economic mechanisms.

**Základy mikroekonomie**

<p class="eyebrow">Teaching fields</p>

## Areas I can teach

::: {.teaching-grid}
::: {.teaching-card}
### European economic history

Industrialisation, globalisation, war, depression, reconstruction, and changing forms of state intervention from the nineteenth century onward.
:::
::: {.teaching-card}
### Monetary and financial history

Gold standards, central banks, banking crises, exchange-rate regimes, inflation, deflation, and the political economy of credibility.
:::
::: {.teaching-card}
### History of economic thought

Competing traditions of value, causality, equilibrium, teleology, and economic order, with particular attention to Central Europe.
:::
::: {.teaching-card}
### Cliometrics and historical data

Turning archival categories into analysable evidence; interpreting regressions historically; communicating uncertainty and sensitivity.
:::
:::
:::

<p class="eyebrow">Approach</p>

## Three habits I want students to acquire
:::
::: {.habit-list}
::: {.habit}
<span>01</span>
<div><strong>Ask what the variable meant historically.</strong> A modern label can conceal a different institution, accounting rule, or population.</div>
:::
::: {.habit}
<span>02</span>
<div><strong>Separate chronology from explanation.</strong> Knowing when a series turned is the beginning of analysis, not its conclusion.</div>
:::
::: {.habit}
<span>03</span>
<div><strong>Treat policy as a constrained choice.</strong> Historical actors faced legal, political, intellectual, and informational limits that a textbook model may omit.</div>
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.page-section .alt-section}
<p class="eyebrow">Supervision and discussion</p>

## Student research

I am especially interested in student projects that combine a clearly bounded historical problem with careful source work: central-bank policy, banking and financial institutions, international trade, interwar Czechoslovakia, historical statistics, or Czech economic thought.

A good project need not begin with sophisticated econometrics. It should begin with a question for which the available evidence can distinguish among competing explanations.
:::
